newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Stocks tumbled on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as players adopted a negative outlook on interest rates, further delays to the abolition of exchange controls and an investigation into foreign exchange forward cover.

- Marlin Granite (Pty) Ltd is poised to buy a 58 percent stake in rival Kudu Granite Holdings Ltd in a deal which will create a combined entity with a market capitalisation of about 300 million rand, producing 40 percent of the sales of the 900,000-tons-a-year local market.
- Funds destined for Malawians employed in South Africa have been diverted by the current and past governments in Lilongwe, a government audit has disclosed.

- Prince Sifiso Zulu resigned as King Goodwill Zwelithini's spokesman saying he was quitting because the monarch was neglecting his official duties despite the fact that he received a "fat" budget from government.
- Eskom, the parastatal electricity company, has delayed the planned launch of a 200 million mark five-year bond to be sold to European investors.

- Tito Mboweni, the labour minister, relegated discriminatory trade union and employer bodies to the annals of history on Monday, and warned that bodies which maintained discrimination in their constitutions would not be registered under the new Labour Relations Act.
- Macadams Bakery Supplies Holdings Ltd is set to bolster its export earnings markedly when negotiations with two international organisations are succesfully concluded.

- As the ANC moved to downplay President Mandela's weekend statement that Deputy President Thabo Mbeki would not necessarily succeed him as leader of the ANC, the organisation's youth wing threw its weight behind Mbeki.
- The gloves are off in the Sandton rates battle, with local government threatening to attach property and cut services if the Sandton Federation of Ratepayers continues "undermining negotiations".
